resources.string: Looking for droplet on your Wi-Fi…
Found on your Wi-Fi: pick your hub
Nothing yet. The hub machine must be on this Wi-Fi with droplet running. Guest networks and some routers block this; enter its address below instead.
This phone can\'t search the Wi-Fi right now. Enter the hub\'s address below.
The hub\'s IP on this Wi-Fi (like 192.168.1.20), or its Tailscale address.

That hub\'s answer doesn\'t match what it announced, so droplet won\'t trust it.
That hub doesn\'t offer droplet\'s secure LAN port (8443). Update droplet on the hub, or use its Tailscale address.

The hub\'s identity changed: it isn\'t using the certificate this phone paired with. Either it\'s not your hub, or its certificate was made again. Pick it below to pair again; you\'ll check a code on one of your devices.
Your other devices will see it by this name on %1$s.
On one of your devices, allow %1$s, and check the code matches.
Waiting for one of your devices…
Can\'t reach the hub right now; still trying…
%1$s wasn\'t allowed in, or the request ran out. Ask again, and allow it on one of your devices.
Not on the same Wi-Fi as %1$s, and Tailscale is off. Connect to your home Wi-Fi, or turn on Tailscale.
Not on the same Wi-Fi as %1$s. Connect to your home Wi-Fi.
droplet tries again by itself when the network changes.
Something at %1$s says it\'s %2$s, but its certificate isn\'t the one this phone paired with. droplet won\'t use it. If you remade the hub\'s certificate, pair again.

droplet forgets the hub, this phone\'s identity on it, and how to reach it. To use it again you\'ll pair again. The hub keeps its files, and this phone stays in its device list until you remove it there.
The hub\'s identity changed, so droplet won\'t use it on the Wi-Fi.
Not named yet. Open droplet and give this phone a name, so other devices can send to it and ring it.
Can\'t reach the hub right now.

Keeps a small notification up and a live connection to the hub, and checks it every 15 seconds, so another device can ring this phone (loud, even on silent) or control it, and you hear about files and messages sent here.
Notify me about files and messages
Needs Stay connected. Shows a notification when something arrives for this phone.
Notifications are off for droplet, so rings and transfers can\'t show.
Show this phone\'s notifications on your other devices, in droplet\'s Phone card. Ongoing ones (music, navigation) are skipped.
Android and MIUI stop apps in the background to save battery, which stops rings getting through.

On Xiaomi / Redmi (MIUI, HyperOS):
1. Autostart: turn it on for droplet.
2. Battery saver: set droplet to No restrictions.
3. Open Recents, long-press droplet and tap the lock, so clearing Recents leaves it alone.
Set droplet\'s battery usage to Unrestricted, so the system doesn\'t stop it.
Battery optimisation is off for droplet.
Battery optimisation is on for droplet.
droplet %1$s · your own hub, no cloud
Ticked apps\' notifications stay on this phone.
Off. Turn on Stay connected so other devices can reach this phone.
Open droplet and name this phone first.
the hub wants its PIN: open droplet and log in
not let in to the hub yet
%1$s is switched off on the phone.
The phone took too long to answer.
Permission not granted on the phone.
The phone wouldn\'t open its messages. On Xiaomi phones, allow droplet to read SMS under Settings → Apps → droplet → Other permissions.
That message is too long for SMS.
The phone refused to send it. On Xiaomi phones, allow Send SMS under Settings → Apps → droplet → Other permissions.
The phone didn\'t confirm sending within 25 seconds. It may still go out. On Xiaomi phones, check Settings → Apps → droplet → Other permissions → Send SMS.
The phone\'s mobile radio is off (airplane mode?).
The phone has no mobile signal right now.
The phone couldn\'t send it (error %1$d). On Xiaomi phones, check Settings → Apps → droplet → Other permissions → Send SMS.

Tap to pause · hold to reset
Volume up: next slide · Volume down: previous
Not connected to the hub. Connect to your home Wi-Fi, or turn on Tailscale.

Other devices can control this phone, and it can drive a computer\'s slides.
Only if this app shows up as a separate device from the one you named in a browser.
On the device you want this app to be, open droplet and make a link code, then type it here.
See what\'s playing here and play, pause, skip, seek and change the volume.
Read this phone\'s text messages and send new ones from the default SIM. Contacts give the names.
Let droplet read and send SMS
Allow SMS (and Contacts) on droplet\'s app page. On Xiaomi phones, also allow Read SMS and Send SMS under Other permissions.
Browse Downloads, Camera, Pictures, Documents, Music and Movies, and take a copy of a file. Nothing else on the phone is reachable.

Text copied on your other devices lands on this phone\'s clipboard. Android only lets the app on screen read the clipboard, so this phone\'s clipboard goes out when you open droplet, or when you tap Send clipboard in the notification or the quick-settings tile.
SMS allowed; contacts not, so no names

To act as a Bluetooth mouse and keyboard, droplet needs Android\'s Nearby devices permission: it connects to a computer or TV you\'ve paired, and makes this phone visible while you pair a new one. droplet doesn\'t scan for or track anything around you.
Allow Nearby devices for droplet on its app page, under Permissions.
Turn it on to use this phone as a mouse and keyboard.
Registering this phone as a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.
Acting as a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse came in Android 9. The presentation remote still works over Wi-Fi with droplet\'s helper.
This phone can\'t be a Bluetooth keyboard

Android on this phone doesn\'t offer the Bluetooth \"HID device\" mode this needs. That\'s up to the phone\'s maker (its firmware), not a setting droplet can change. The presentation remote still works over Wi-Fi with droplet\'s helper.
The phone wouldn\'t let droplet be a keyboard
Another app may be using this phone as a Bluetooth keyboard or mouse right now: close it and try again. If this keeps happening, this phone\'s firmware doesn\'t allow the mode.
Pick a paired computer or TV below, or pair a new one. A computer or TV can also connect to this phone by itself while this screen is open.
Pair this phone from the computer or TV (the steps are below). It connects by itself once paired. Keep this screen open meanwhile.
Its Bluetooth must be on, and it must be within a few metres.
Check its Bluetooth is on. If it was paired with this phone before, for music or calls, it may not know the phone can be a keyboard: remove this phone from its Bluetooth list and pair again.
Pair a new computer or TV
The phone stayed hidden. Try again, or pair from the phone\'s own Bluetooth settings.
Make the phone visible, then on the other device:
Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Add device → Bluetooth. Pick this phone and confirm the code on both.
System Settings → Bluetooth → Add New Device (or the Bluetooth icon in the panel). Pick this phone and confirm the code.
Settings → Remotes & Accessories → Pair remote or accessory. Pick this phone and confirm.
Paired before, for music or calls? Remove this phone on that device first, then pair again, so it learns the phone can be a keyboard.
Slide to move · tap to click\nTwo fingers: scroll or right-click\nDouble-tap and hold: drag
Types as a US keyboard. A Bluetooth keyboard sends key positions, not letters, so non-English characters may not type, and a computer set to another layout may show other symbols.
Skipped \"%1$s\": a Bluetooth keyboard types by key position, and the US layout has no key for it.
Home and Back work on Google TV and Android. The volume keys change the TV\'s or computer\'s volume.
Pair a computer or TV over Bluetooth…
Bluetooth isn\'t ready: open Mouse & keyboard to fix it.
Use this phone as a Bluetooth mouse, keyboard and media remote for a computer or TV. Nothing to install on it, and no Wi-Fi needed.
